name: No Renunciaré AI Trend: Sing the Bolero With a Giant Mustache
blurb: The No Renunciaré trend is an AI singing clip from October 2026: you sing a dramatic bolero into a vintage chrome microphone on three stages, completely serious, and a man gets a giant curled mustache.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 15 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A dramatic old-school bolero performance in three shots on three stages, vertical 9:16, 15 seconds, filmed like a polished TV music show: photorealistic, sharp, cinematic light. The singer sings a slow romantic ballad into a vintage chrome microphone with huge, over-the-top emotion, completely serious, like a 1970s crooner.

The singer is the person in [Image 1], in every shot: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles), the same build and the clothes from [Image 1], so their friends recognize them at once. The same face from the first frame to the last, also with the eyes closed and the head tilted back. Never morph. If [Image 1] shows a man, he wears a giant, glossy handlebar mustache in his own hair color, much wider than his face, with big round curls at both tips (it takes the place of any mustache he has; a beard stays). A woman keeps her own face with no mustache. If [Image 1] shows an animal, the singer is that animal sitting upright and holding the microphone in its front paws, with its own face, fur and markings, not a person.

Shot 1 (0-5 s): a small stage in front of a warm wall of horizontal light-wood slats, soft golden light. A medium shot from the waist up, seen a little from the side: the singer holds the vintage chrome microphone on its stand close to the lips, eyes closed, chin up, and sings with deep feeling; at about 3.5 s one arm rises high above the head, palm open.
Shot 2 (5-10 s): a hard cut to a close-up from the chest up in front of a plain, bright blue studio backdrop, even light. The singer holds the chrome microphone right at the mouth and sings toward the camera, eyes half closed, eyebrows lifted, small shakes of the head on the long notes. The face is large and sharp.
Shot 3 (10-15 s): a hard cut to a dark stage with one bright spotlight from above and behind, a white rim light on the hair and shoulders, a light haze. A medium shot: the singer sings into a chrome microphone on a stand, leans back on the big final note, sweeps one arm up over the head and holds the note, eyes closed.

Audio: a slow, dramatic romantic bolero ballad in Spanish with a lush 1970s orchestra: strings, a soft nylon-string guitar and light drums. The singer sings it live in their own voice, with big emotion and a long held last note; the mouth moves with every sung word. The words are original Spanish love lines: "Amor, amor, mi corazón es tuyo, contigo me quedaré hasta el final; no hay noche sin tu luz, amor." No other voices, no speech, no applause.

Exactly one singer and one microphone in every shot, no band, no audience in view. One head, two arms, five fingers on each hand; the microphone never merges with the hand or the face. No team or brand logo, no lettering on the clothes, no text, no captions, no subtitles, no watermark.
